Metadata.title: 3D Print Cost Calculator
Metadata.description: Work out what a 3D print really costs: filament, electricity, printer wear, hardware like keyrings and magnets, labor and failed prints. Free and open source.

Header.localModeHint: Running on your own machine. Everything is saved to this instance.
Header.guestHint: Your work is saved to this browser. Sign in to keep it on any device.

Home.title: Know what every print really costs
Home.lead: Filament is only part of the bill. Add electricity, printer wear, glue, keyrings, magnets, packaging, your time and the prints that fail, and get a price you can actually sell at.
Home.exampleTitle: Example: a keychain, 12 g of PLA, 48 minutes

counts.filament: Filament by the gram, with waste from purges and supports
counts.machine: Electricity, printer depreciation and maintenance per print hour
counts.extras: Your own list of extras: keyrings, magnets, inserts, glue, paint, boxes
counts.labor: Preparation and post-processing time at your hourly rate
counts.business: Failure rate, overhead, profit margin, VAT and marketplace fees

SignIn.title: Sign in

SignIn.guestNote: You can also keep calculating without an account.
SignIn.localMode: This instance runs in local mode, so there is nothing to sign in to. Everything you save stays on this machine.

Library.title: Library
Library.lead: Save your printers, filaments and extras once, then pick them in every calculation.

printers.empty: No printers yet. Add the one you print with to count electricity and wear.

fields.name: Name
fields.nameHint: What you call it, e.g. "P1S in the office".
fields.resaleValueHint: What you expect to sell it for at the end. Leave empty if you'll use it until it dies.
fields.lifetimeHoursHint: Print hours you expect before replacing it. 3,000–8,000 h is common for hobby FDM printers.
fields.powerWattsHint: While printing, including the heated bed. Check a smart plug, or the spec sheet (often 100–350 W).
fields.maintenanceCostPerHourHint: Nozzles, build plates, belts, lubricant, spread per print hour.

filaments.empty: No filaments yet. Add the spools you buy so prints are costed by the gram.

fields.name: Name
fields.spoolWeightGramsHint: Filament only, without the spool. Usually 1000 g.

extras.empty: No extras yet. Add keyrings, magnets, inserts, glue or packaging you put into prints.

Settings.title: Settings
Settings.lead: These values fill in every new calculation. You can still change them for a single print.
Settings.notSavedYet: These are starting values. Save to make them yours.

fields.currencyHint: Used for every price you enter. Amounts aren't converted.
fields.electricityPricePerKwhHint: Per kWh, from your bill, taxes included.
fields.laborRatePerHourHint: What an hour of your time is worth. Use 0 to leave labor out.
fields.filamentWastePctHint: Purges, skirts and test lines on top of what the slicer reports.
fields.failureRatePctHint: Share of prints that fail and get reprinted.
fields.overheadPctHint: Rent, software, tools and other running costs, as a share of production cost.
fields.taxRatePctHint: Added to the price the buyer pays. Use 0 if you don't charge it.
fields.marketplaceFeePctHint: Commission taken from the price the buyer pays.
fields.businessNameHint: Printed at the top of your PDF quotes. You can change it on each quote.

profitModes.MARKUP_hint: A cost of {cost} with {pct} markup sells for {price}.
profitModes.MARGIN_hint: A cost of {cost} with {pct} margin sells for {price}.

Calculator.title: Calculator
Calculator.lead: Describe one print job. The cost and the suggested price update as you type.

fields.piecesPerJobHint: How many identical pieces come out of one print (one plate).
fields.quantityHint: The size of the order. Order totals use this.

printer.label: Printer
printer.summary: {watts} W. Wear and maintenance: {wear} per print hour.
printer.resaleValue: Resale value at end of life
printer.lifetimeHoursHint: Print hours before it is worn out. 3,000 to 8,000 is common for hobby printers.
printer.saveHint: Want this filled in for you? Add your printers to the <link>library</link>.

filament.label: Filament {n}
filament.name: Name
filament.hint: Enter the weight your slicer reports, supports included. {waste}% is added for purges and skirts.

extras.label: Extra
extras.empty: Keyrings, magnets, glue, a gift box? Add anything that goes into each finished piece.
extras.quantityHint: How many go into one piece. Fractions are fine.
extras.name: Name

labor.prepHint: Slicing and starting the print. Once per print, shared by its pieces.
labor.postHint: Supports, sanding, assembly, packing. For every piece.

business.lead: These start from your <link>settings</link>. Change them here for this calculation only.
business.failureHint: Share of prints that fail and must be redone.
business.overheadHint: Rent, software, tools. Added on top of the cost.
business.feeHint: Taken from the price the buyer pays.

result.title: Result
result.empty: Enter the print time and the filament weight to see the cost.
result.badNumber: One of the numbers can't be read. Check the fields marked in red.
result.badMargin: A margin has to be below 100%. Use a markup for higher profits.
result.badFee: VAT and the marketplace fee together leave nothing of the price.
result.badRange: One of the values is out of range. Check the fields.

import.hint: G-code or a sliced 3MF. It is read in your browser and never uploaded.
import.multi: {count} filaments found. They were added as separate rows.
import.estimated: The file only gives the filament length, so the weight is an estimate for 1.75 mm filament. Check it against your slicer.
import.noTime: The print time wasn't in the file. Enter it yourself.
import.noWeight: The filament weight wasn't in the file. Enter it yourself.

errors.unsupported: This file type isn't supported. Use .gcode or .3mf.
errors.binaryGcode: This is a binary G-code file (.bgcode). In PrusaSlicer, turn off "Binary G-code" in Printer Settings, General, and export again.
errors.tooLarge: This file is too large to read in the browser.
errors.unreadable: This file couldn't be read. It may be damaged.
errors.noData: This G-code has no slicer summary, so there is nothing to read. Enter the numbers from your slicer.
errors.unsliced3mf: This 3MF only holds the model. Slice it and export the sliced file or the G-code.
